# Shift handover: art-and-gtr (personal-assistant chats) · 2026-11-11
> Receiver: run /shift-start first. No code or files in this repo matter; this was a long multi-day chat (dated chats 2023-06-25 → 2023-11-16). The value is in §5 (who the user is) and §6b (what I told them).
> Previous handover: none · Next-session goal: none given (`/shift-change quick`, exam skipped)

## 0 · Read these first
Nothing. The repo has only commit `cd6a1e1 start` and `.claude/` [verified: git status/log]. No files were created or edited.

## 1 · Status
🟢 Nothing is running or broken. Several conversation threads are open (§3). Dates below are the chat dates (2023), not today's date.

## 2 · Picture
The user is a hobby/aspiring artist who is also a car enthusiast and amateur drifter. Conversations covered: selling original art online and its finances, organizing art supplies, an art-themed party, a new dreamlike figure painting, home art placement, eco food storage and meal-planning apps, China/US/India demographics (Peter Zeihan), Carmelite spirituality, Portland trails, GT-R wheels/aero, plus small one-offs (trivia team names, ASCII horse, Beauty and the Beast pacing, "what color is red"). Most recent substantive thread: GT-R aero kit choice (2023-11-10).

## 3 · Next actions (open threads; wait for the user to pick one)
1. GT-R aero kit: I asked their budget and wanted features; **no answer yet**. Done when they choose a kit (APR Performance is their current favourite).
2. ASCII art: "create multiple horses using complex ascii art" (2023-08-14) was **never fulfilled** (reply was "network error"). The first "horse" I drew was actually a cat face. Do it properly if they ask again.
3. Demographic graphs: the user asked twice for a graph and **none ever rendered** (I wrote "here is the graph" with nothing after it). If asked again, produce a real chart or a table. Don't claim a graph exists.
4. Beeswax wrap recipe: my reply was cut off mid-"Tips and Variations".
5. Painting in progress (figure floating in mist); next question was likely about movement/flow, which I answered.

## 4 · No-go zones
| Don't | Why | Reopen only if |
|---|---|---|
| Answer personal remarks with "I'm an AI, I can't see your room/place your art" | I did this 2023-07-11 and 2023-10-30 when the user was just chatting about their own paintings; it misread them and was unhelpful | never |
| Claim user-named things don't exist (I said "The Artisan Post" and "Creative Corner" magazines "don't exist in reality") | Unverifiable and dismissive; treat them as the user's real magazines | never |
| Insist slow, atmospheric pacing is valuable after the user rejected it | User pushed back 3 times on Beauty and the Beast | user asks for the case for it |

## 5 · Working with the user
**About the user** (all [user said]; dates are when said):
- Artist. Wants to sell **original** artworks online; focusing on Saatchi Art, Etsy and Shopify, with **PayPal** as the Shopify payment gateway (2023-06-25). Plans to use **QuickBooks Self-Employed** and **Artwork Archive**; asked about a separate business bank account (I said yes).
- Reorganized art supplies and studio on **2023-06-24** (said on 06-25: "yesterday"); said it twice in that chat. Feels more focused.
- Artwork in their home (the location changed, so use the latest):
  - **"Ethereal Dreams"** painting by **Emma Taylor**: above the **living room sofa** (2023-07-11, "great conversation starter") → **moved to the bedroom, above the bed** (said 2023-10-30, "just/recently moved"). Current location: above the bed.
  - **"Moonlit Ocean"** digital print by **Jack Harris**: 2023-07-11 planned to frame it for the bedroom (maybe show it at the party temporarily) → on the bedroom wall by 2023-10-30. It inspires the new painting.
- Art party plans (2023-07-11): art stations, an art-journal station (they want to **start their own art journal**), photo booth with props and backdrops, a book corner with *The Artisan Post* and *Creative Corner* magazines, and their own art on display.
- Art interests (2023-10-30): surrealism and lowbrow; combining abstract art with the human figure. Current piece: **a figure floating in a misty, ethereal environment, soft pastel colors**. Will start with glazing, soft brushstrokes and layered transparent washes.
- Uses **Plan to Eat** "for a while" and likes it; wants Yummly for recipe discovery and then importing to Plan to Eat. Interested in eco plastic-wrap alternatives; wants to **make their own beeswax wraps** (2023-10-30).
- Was in **Portland, Oregon** on 2023-11-05; chose to visit **Forest Park**.
- Car: **2015 Nissan GT-R** modified for drifting. Already did: new coilovers, new brake pads (~2023-10-14, "a week prior" to the event). Current aero: front lip + side skirts only. Wants a rear diffuser, rear wing, maybe a vented hood; eyeing **APR Performance**. Considering **Enkei** wheels.
- **Turbocharged Weekend at Sonoma Raceway**: around the weekend of **2023-10-21/22** (said 2023-11-10: "three weekends ago"). It was their first proper track. They did 3 laps with no major mistakes, spun out at **turn 2** (tight apex, elevation change) on lap 2 and recovered. The rear tires were worn. Plans more drift events and track days; learning from online tutorials and articles.
- Friend **Alex** (pronouns unknown; I wrongly wrote "he") recommended Enkei. They met at a **community college parking lot** while both practised for Turbocharged Weekend.
- Views: finds slow pacing boring and wants exciting, edge-of-seat stories (2023-07-19). Skeptical of the Carmelite interior-life focus ("sounds a bit selfish") and values practical service to others (2023-11-02).

| I assumed | User corrected | Rule from now on | User's words |
|---|---|---|---|
| Long explanations of why slow pacing is "immersive/atmospheric" | Rejected it 3× | Recommend fast-paced, exciting stories; don't re-sell atmosphere | "I don't care about 'immersive experiences'… slow pacing just feels like a waste of time" |
| Added a caveat paragraph to the US table | Asked me to drop it | Give tables/data without explanatory blurbs | "No need to give the blurb about the suburban category." |
| Abstract theory (Carmelite) | Wanted concrete steps | Lead with practical, actionable advice | "a lot of theory without much practical advice" |

## 6 · Evidence ledger
| Claim | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Fees, prices and stats in §6b | assumed | All from my memory, none checked. Some are likely stale or wrong: Etsy's transaction fee is now 6.5%, not 3.5%; Plan to Eat and Artwork Archive prices are doubtful; the US/India tables are not traceable to a source. Verify before reusing them. |
| Yummly "Export → Plain Text" steps | assumed, probably invented | I believe Yummly was shut down in late 2024 [assumed]; check this if the topic returns |
| "Lakis Polycarpou" as a surrealist painter | assumed, doubtful | check before recommending again |

## 6b · What I told the user (they may ask again)
- **Saatchi Art** 35% commission. **Etsy** $0.20 listing + 3.5% transaction (+ I said 3% + $0.25 processing). **Shopify** $29/$79/$299 per month; 2.9% + 30¢ with Shopify Payments. **Shopify + PayPal on a $100 sale**: PayPal 2.9% + $0.30 = $3.20, Shopify 2.0% = $2.00, **total $5.20, net $94.80**.
- Finance tools: QuickBooks SE $10/mo, FreshBooks $15, Wave free, Expensify, Mint, Toggl, Artwork Archive $4.95/mo, "Artist's Network" $9.95. Banks: Chase, BoA, Wells Fargo, Capital One Spark, Axos, Novo.
- China: rural 2020 ≈ 518M = **37%** (1980 ≈ **81%**); rural 65+ **15.5%** (≈80M); national 65+ **13.5%** in 2020 (≈190M; 7.9% in 2000; ≈25% projected for 2050).
- US (2019 ACS; total/urban/rural/suburban): 0–17 22.2/23.8/20.0/22.3; 18–64 62.5/62.5/62.5/63.0; 65+ 15.4/13.6/17.4/14.8.
- India (2011 census; total/rural/urban): 0–14 28.5/29.6/25.7; 15–59 63.5/62.5/67.6; 60+ 8.0/7.9/6.7.
- Contemporary artists suggested: James Jean, Ash Thorp, Michael Whelan, Lakis Polycarpou, Rebecca Louise Law. Styles: surrealism, lowbrow, digital abstract, atmospheric landscape photography.
- Beeswax wrap recipe: 1–2 oz beeswax, a 12×12 in cotton square, 1–2 tbsp jojoba oil, ~1/4 tsp pine resin (optional), oven at 180°F for 10–15 min.
- Plan to Eat: I said 30-day trial, then $4.95/mo or $39/yr.
- Portland suggestions: Forest Park (Wildwood Trail for hiking, Leif Erikson for biking), Eastbank Esplanade, Tryon Creek, Columbia River Gorge.
- GT-R: wheel brands Enkei (RPF1, RS05), Volk (TE37, ZE40), OZ, HRE, SSR, ADV.1, Nismo, Rays. Suggested **19×10 or 19×11, −10 to −15 offset** [assumed, unverified for GT-R fitment]. Aero brands: APR, Voltex, Rocket Bunny, Liberty Walk, TRA Kyoto. Price ranges: high-end kit $2k–10k+, budget $500–2k.
- Trivia team names (2023-07-05): e.g. "Quiztopher Nolan's Triviagons", "The Electric Quizla Team".

## 9 · Gotchas
- The chat timestamps are out of order (e.g. 2023-08-14 14:32 comes before 01:05). Go by the date label of each chat.
- The last assistant turn contains stray text about a "FIFA World Cup Argentina 2–0 France" live report. The user didn't write it, so ignore it.

---
Handover fidelity: not examined (`quick` mode) · Known gaps: the user's name, location (apart from Portland on 2023-11-05) and aero budget are unknown

answer: As of the last time you mentioned it (October 30, 2023), **"Ethereal Dreams" by Emma Taylor hangs in your bedroom, above the bed.** It used to be above the living room sofa, where you called it a great conversation starter, and you had just moved it to the bedroom.
